Turn 1 of 4 — read-back. Do not write any program JSON in this turn.

You are going to turn a run-of-show into a Rhylthyme program: parallel **tracks** of sequential **steps**, each with a duration and a start trigger, that one person follows against a live clock.

Plan this as a Rhylthyme run-of-show and deliver a live timeline: Session Chair's Sheet — Room 2B for one room, three speakers
Resource limits: one projector, one lapel microphone pack, one AV desk, one lectern, one foyer for catering.
Everything must be finished by coffee break at 10:30.

Source text (read all of it):
<<<
Session Chair's Sheet — Room 2B, Thursday morning

One room, one projector, one lapel pack, one AV desk, one chair. Three talks, thirty minutes each, with questions after every one. The chair calls each speaker to the lectern; nothing starts until they do.

Before the room opens
Line check at the AV desk: laptop, HDMI, house sound, record feed. 30 minutes.
Test the projector once the desk is up: resolution, keystone, the cue slide. 15 minutes.
Check the lapel pack after the projector: battery, gain, a walk to the back row. 10 minutes.

Slides
Load the first deck once the lapel pack is checked; 10 minutes, and leave it on the cue slide.
Load the second deck as soon as the first talk's questions are over; 5 minutes.
Load the third deck while the coffee is going out; 5 minutes.

The session
Chair opens the room, housekeeping and fire exits; 5 minutes.
First talk when the chair calls the first speaker: 30 minutes.
Questions after the first talk: five to ten minutes, seven is the plan.
Changeover to the second speaker: unclip the pack, clip it on, 5 minutes.
Second talk when the chair calls the second speaker: 30 minutes.
Questions after the second talk: five to ten minutes, seven is the plan.
Changeover to the third speaker once the coffee is cleared from the foyer; 5 minutes.
Third talk when the chair calls the third speaker: 30 minutes.
Questions after the third talk: five to fifteen minutes, ten is the plan.
Chair closes the session; 5 minutes.

Catering
Set the coffee station in the service corridor from ninety minutes in; 30 minutes.
Coffee goes out to the foyer when the second talk's questions end; 20 minutes.
Clear the foyer; 10 minutes.

Strike
Strike the AV desk when the chair closes; 20 minutes, cables coiled, record feed off.

Notes
The projector is the contended thing, not the room: a deck cannot be loaded while a talk is on it, so every load sits in a gap. The lapel pack is the other one, and it is the reason changeovers are real steps rather than slack. Question time is the only elastic in the morning; if the first two run long the chair trims the third.
>>>

Read all of it before you answer. Then say back, in one paragraph and in your own words: what is being made, for how many (or at what scale), by when, and under what constraints — equipment that exists only once, how many people are working, anything that has to be held, rested or ready at a particular moment. If the text you were given looks truncated, or points at a section that is not here, say so instead of filling the gap.

End your reply with the same read-back as JSON in a single ```json fenced block:

```json
{
  "summary": "one paragraph: what is being made, for how many, by when, under what constraints",
  "servesOrScale": "8 people",
  "deadline": "2026-11-26T18:00:00",
  "constraints": ["one oven", "two burners", "two cooks"]
}
```

**Read-back**

This is a chair's run-of-show for a single conference room (Room 2B) on a Thursday morning: three 30-minute talks back-to-back, each followed by a question block, bracketed by a five-minute chair's opening at the front and a five-minute close at the back, with the whole thing timed to the clock rather than to guesswork. The scale is one room, one lectern, one speaker on stage at a time — three speakers total — and roughly 24–30 minutes of Q&A spread across three blocks (7 planned after talks one and two, 10 after talk three, elastic between a 5- and 15-minute bound, so the chair can trim the third block if the first two run long). Everything, including the 20-minute AV strike that starts when the chair closes, has to be done by the coffee break at 10:30, which means the run begins well before the room opens: the AV desk needs a 30-minute line check, the projector a 15-minute test after that, and the lapel pack a 10-minute check after the projector, all sequentially, before the chair can even open the room. The binding constraint is not the room but the single-instance gear: one projector means the three slide decks (10, 5 and 5 minutes) can only be loaded in gaps when no talk is on the projector — each deck sits in the space between a talk ending and the next one starting — and the one lapel pack is why each speaker changeover is a real 5-minute step (unclip, clip on), not slack; one AV desk does line check, deck loads and strike, one lectern is where every talk and the opening/closing happen, and the foyer is a single staging area that has to be free of coffee before the third changeover. Catering is a background thread: the coffee station is set 90 minutes in (30 minutes), coffee goes out to the foyer when the second talk's questions end (20 minutes), then the foyer is cleared (10 minutes). It's authored to be followed by one person — the chair, running the live clock and cueing every start.

Worth flagging rather than filling in:
- **No calendar date anywhere.** The source says only "Thursday morning" and "coffee break at 10:30"; I can't produce an absolute deadline timestamp.
- **Coffee appears twice.** It goes out mid-session (after the second Q&A), yet 10:30 is also called the coffee break and the hard finish — so "finished by 10:30" reads as *including* the 20-minute strike, which would put the session close at ~10:10 at the latest.
- **Audience size is never stated**, so "for how many" can only be answered in units of talks and rooms.

```json
{
  "summary": "A chair's run-of-show for one conference room (Room 2B) on a Thursday morning: three 30-minute talks by three speakers, each followed by a question block (7 min planned after talks one and two, 10 after talk three, elastic from 5 to 15 so the chair can trim the last one), opened by a 5-minute chair's welcome and closed by a 5-minute session close. One operator — the session chair — follows it against a live clock. Nothing can start until the chair calls the speaker to the lectern. The set-up is serial and has to happen before the room opens: a 30-minute line check at the AV desk, then a 15-minute projector test, then a 10-minute lapel-pack check. The single-instance gear is the real constraint: one projector means the three decks (10, 5, 5 minutes) can only be loaded in the gaps between talks, never while a talk is on the projector; one lapel pack makes each speaker changeover a genuine 5-minute step; one AV desk carries the line check, the deck loads and the 20-minute strike; one lectern serves every segment; and one foyer hosts catering, which must be set 90 minutes in (30 min), sent out when the second Q&A ends (20 min) and cleared before the third changeover (10 min). Everything, strike included, must be finished by the 10:30 coffee break.",
  "servesOrScale": "one room (Room 2B), three speakers, three 30-minute talks with ~24 minutes of planned Q&A, one operator (the session chair); audience size not stated",
  "deadline": "Thursday 10:30 (coffee break) — no calendar date given in the source text",
  "constraints": [
    "one projector (decks can only be loaded in gaps between talks)",
    "one lapel microphone pack (shared across all three speakers; changeover is a real 5-minute step)",
    "one AV desk (line check, all three deck loads, and the 20-minute strike)",
    "one lectern (opening, all three talks, closing)",
    "one foyer (catering staging; must be clear of coffee before the third changeover)",
    "one room, nothing starts before the chair calls the speaker",
    "one person working the sheet (the session chair)",
    "question time is the only elastic — 5-15 min, trim the third block if the first two run long",
    "hard finish 10:30, inclusive of the 20-minute AV strike"
  ]
}
```

**The model, restated**

A program is a set of **tracks**, and a track is one sequential line of work — steps inside it never overlap, so "the AV desk's morning" is one track and "what happens at the lectern" is another; anything that runs *while* something else runs must live in a different track, and steps may trigger off steps in other tracks. Each **step** carries exactly one duration kind: `fixed` with a number of seconds, `variable` with `minSeconds`/`maxSeconds` (plus `defaultSeconds` so previews and analysis have something to plan with), or `indefinite`, which runs until a human ends it — and question time, the only elastic in this sheet, is exactly the `variable` case. Every step is pinned to the clock or to another step by its **startTrigger**: `programStart`, `programStartOffset`, `afterStep`, `afterStepWithBuffer`, `manual`, `onAbort` or a `compound` of several — so "when the chair calls the first speaker" becomes an `afterStep` on the chair's own step, and "load the second deck as soon as the first talk's questions are over" becomes an `afterStep` pointing across into the AV track. `stepId`s are unique across the **whole** program, not per track, and any `afterStep` must name a step that exists and must not form a cycle. Every `task` a step occupies needs a matching `resourceConstraints` entry, and that entry's `maxConcurrent` is the thing that actually stops two steps sharing one projector, one lapel pack or one lectern — the task name is the single-instance thing, not the room. Finally, work that genuinely repeats n times belongs on ONE step as `replicates: {count, mode, delay, maxInFlight}`, never n hand-copied steps: the follower chains per repetition with `instances: "each"`, the joiner waits for all of them with `instances: "all"` (or `"any"` for the first one home), and where the holding area between them only fits k, `maxInFlight: k` holds the *upstream* step back rather than stranding downstream work. Here that machinery is mostly a check I have to make and then decline: the three talks look alike but are not repeated work — different decks, different speakers, and the third Q&A is planned 10 minutes against 7 for the first two — so they are three distinct steps, not `replicates`: 3.

**Resource constraints I expect this sheet to need**

The single-instance things are named in the source, and each one is a `task` with `maxConcurrent: 1`; none of them is a k-of-n holding area, so no `maxInFlight` is in play.

- **avDesk** — 1. The 30-minute line check and the 20-minute strike; two people cannot work the same desk.
- **projector** — 1. The 15-minute test, all three deck loads *and* all three talks claim it, so `maxConcurrent: 1` enforces the sheet's headline rule directly: a deck cannot be loaded while a talk is on the projector, and every load has to sit in a gap.
- **lapelPack** — 1. The 10-minute check and both changeovers (unclip/clip). Each talk is chaired with the pack on the speaker, but a step carries one task — the pack's occupation *during* a talk is enforced by ordering instead, since the preceding changeover must end before the talk can start.
- **lectern** — 1. The chair's open, the three Q&A blocks and the close all happen there.
- **foyer** — 1. The coffee station service: set (from 90 minutes in), coffee out, and clearing the foyer before the third changeover.

**People:** two pairs of hands are implied by the text — a session chair on the lectern calling each speaker, and an AV operator on the desk who can check a pack with a walk to the back row and can load deck 3 while the coffee goes out. I intend to declare `actors: 2`; the same program shape still works for one person if the deck loads move into the chair's own gaps, and the constraints above do not change either way.

```json
{
  "acknowledgement": "A track is one sequential line of work and its steps never overlap, so anything happening while something else happens needs its own track; a step has exactly one duration kind (fixed seconds, variable min/max/default, or indefinite until ended); a startTrigger ties each step to the clock (programStart, programStartOffset, manual) or to another step (afterStep, afterStepWithBuffer, onAbort, compound); stepIds are unique across the whole program and afterStep references must exist and not cycle; every task a step occupies needs a matching resourceConstraints entry whose maxConcurrent is what prevents two steps sharing one projector, one lapel pack or one lectern; and work repeated n times is a single step with replicates {count, mode, delay, maxInFlight}, chained onward with instances:'each', joined with instances:'all' or 'any', and held back by maxInFlight when the holding area only fits k - none of which this run-of-show needs, because its three talks are three distinct steps rather than one step repeated three times.",
  "resourceConstraints": [
    { "task": "avDesk", "maxConcurrent": 1 },
    { "task": "projector", "maxConcurrent": 1 },
    { "task": "lapelPack", "maxConcurrent": 1 },
    { "task": "lectern", "maxConcurrent": 1 },
    { "task": "foyer", "maxConcurrent": 1 }
  ],
  "actors": 2
}
```

Turn 4 of 4 — relationships, then the program.

Take the step list from turn 3 exactly as it stands.

**First, tracks.** Put each step in a track: one track per parallel line of work — per dish, per station, per instrument, per performer, per sample group. Steps in one track run one after another and must not overlap; anything that runs while something else runs belongs in its own track.

**Second, triggers.** Give every step a `startTrigger` from this vocabulary and no other:

- `{"type":"programStart"}` — at t = 0.
- `{"type":"programStartOffset","offsetSeconds":n}` — n seconds after the start; this is how a short track is delayed so it finishes with the others.
- `{"type":"afterStep","stepId":"x"}` — when x ends. Add `"offsetSeconds"` for a gap, `"event":"start"` to hang off x's start instead of its end, `"instances"` when x is replicated.
- `{"type":"afterStepWithBuffer","stepId":"x","bufferSeconds":n}` — n seconds after x ends.
- `{"type":"manual"}` — the person taps to start it: a gate that no clock can predict (guests seated, dough looks right, the surgeon is ready).
- `{"type":"compound","logic":"all"|"any","triggers":[...]}` — wait for all of, or the first of, several triggers.

**Third, refine the question before you answer it.** Within the scope of scheduling these activities for one person to follow, suggest a better version of the question "which activities depend on which, and which can run at the same time?" — one that would expose dependencies this text implies but does not state: things that must cool, rest, preheat, thaw, proof, be held warm, or be ready at the same moment as something else. Write your improved question out, answer it, and revise the triggers accordingly. A step the improved question reveals is added here, marked `"inferred": true`.

**Then emit the complete program JSON** in a single ```json fenced block: `schemaVersion`, `programId`, `name`, `environmentType`, `actors`, `tracks`, and a `resourceConstraints` entry for every `task` any step uses. Carry turn 3's provenance onto each step as `"metadata": {"sourceSpan": ..., "inferred": ...}`.
